questions.problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
3,\,1,\,15,\,3,\,2,\,12
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ is the mean of the data set.

First, we need to compute the mean. There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (3+1+15+3+2+12) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 36 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(3-6)^{2}+(1-6)^{2}+(15-6)^{2}+(3-6)^{2}+(2-6)^{2}+(12-6)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[9+25+81+9+16+36] \\  & =\frac{176}{6} \\  & =\frac{88}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i}=-30,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i}^{2}=120.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=15$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i}=-30,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{15}{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{15}\cdot (-30) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i}^{2}=120,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{15}{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{15}\cdot 120 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =8-{(-2)}^{2} \\  & =8-4 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance Given the Number, Sum, and Sum of Squares of the Data Points
canonical_examples.problem:
Compute the variance $\sigma^2$ of a data set $x_i$ consisting of $8$ data points, where

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
\sigma^2 = \overline{x^2} - (\overline{x})^2,
$$

where $\overline{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overline{x^2}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, and we know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 40 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ We know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 320 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =40-{(5)}^{2} \\  & =40-25 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot ({4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (16+25+16+49+64+121+9) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 300 \\  & =\frac{300}{7}.\end{aligned}

$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 } = \sqrt{ \,\,\, \vphantom{\sum\limits_{i=1}^n} \overline{x^2} - \left( \overline{x} \right)^2 }
$$

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (7+5+0+2+1+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 18 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (49+25+0+4+1+9) \\  & =\frac{88}{6} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-9 \\  & =\frac{44-27}{3} \\  & =\frac{17}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{17}{3} }.
$$
